title: VPC Audit Bridge: Flexible customer-blob forwarding + retention controls
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Private/VPC and on-prem customers need an auditable, configurable way to forward Redwood audit logs to customer-managed object storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with clear retention and encryption guarantees. Current options are ad-hoc and either require customers to accept Redwood-managed credentials or to run custom agents. Goal: deliver three interoperable forwarding modes with policy controls, retention metadata, and minimal attack surface for credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Provide three supported forwarding modes: (1) Pre-signed upload URLs generated by a local agent (air-gapped friendly), (2) Server-side direct upload via STS/AssumeRole where customer's cloud identity is used but credentials never persist in the control plane, and (3) Push endpoint with mutual-TLS for customers that provide an HTTPS ingest endpoint.
Audit entries are exported in NDJSON with per-entry metadata fields for tenant, region, model, and sequence_id. Each file chunk must include a manifest allowing deterministic replay.

Support per-tenant retention policy metadata surfaced in the Console and enforced by optional lifecycle hints included in manifests (implementation leaves actual deletion to customer storage or an optional Redwood-managed lifecycle job when explicitly enabled).
All transfers must be TLS encrypted in transit and signed; server-side uploads use short-lived credentials (<=15m). No long-lived customer credentials are stored in Redwood control plane.
Provide comprehensive observability: per-forwarding-path metrics (bytes, event counts, failures), per-file checksums, and DLQ for failed uploads with 7-day retain in private deployment for recovery.
E2E tests across S3/GCS/Azure with 99th-percentile upload latency targets documented and verified in the CI harness.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (agent + presigned): Build lightweight forwarder binary for private deployments that batches audit lines to ndjson.gz, requests presigned URL from local control-plane component, and uploads with retry/backoff. Implement manifest format and chunking.

Phase 2 (server-side STS): Implement assume-role flow for AWS and comparable short-lived access flows for GCP/Azure. Add connector code to upload directly from control plane in Private mode without persisting credentials; keys rotated per-upload window.
Phase 3 (mTLS push): Add configurable push endpoint support with mTLS credential exchange and backpressure signals. Provide Console UI for endpoint health and cert rotation.

Phase 4 (retention & lifecycle): Surface per-tenant retention hints, optional Redwood-managed lifecycle worker for customers who opt-in, and documentation for customers who prefer storage lifecycle rules.
Phase 5 (QA & rollout): End-to-end tests, security review, invite 2 pilot customers, iterate on failure modes and observability, then GA.
Implementation owners: Ethan (lead eng), Aisha Khan (infra), Liam Patel (security), Priya Rao (PM liaison).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Pre-signed approach is air-gap friendly and minimizes control-plane exposure but pushes retry complexity to the forwarder agent and requires customer-managed upload endpoints.

Server-side STS is simplest for customers on public clouds but increases control-plane bandwidth usage; mitigate by performing uploads within customer VPC in Private deployments to avoid public egress where possible.

Storing long-lived credentials in the control plane is unacceptable from a compliance perspective; decision: persist only non-sensitive metadata and ephemeral session tokens (<=15m) in-memory or Ephemeral KMS-wrapped caches where required.
We will not attempt to auto-delete customer data across cloud providers; Redwood can optionally run lifecycle jobs only when explicit customer consent is recorded in service agreement.
security_considerations: All upload flows must be authenticated and authorized against tenant-level RBAC v2 roles; only 'audit-admin' and 'audit-export' roles can configure sinks.
mTLS endpoints require cert pinning and rotation workflows surfaced in Console; support for customer-supplied CA bundles for air-gapped deployments.
Audit transport must include HMAC of each chunk using a per-tenant key stored in the customer's KMS when available; fallback to ephemeral signing keys with rotation logs.

Threat model reviewed with Security: risks include credential exfiltration, replay attacks, and metasessions. Mitigations: ephemeral credentials, per-chunk nonces, manifest checksums, and mandatory audit trail for sink config changes.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal dogfood in Private dev cluster, verify uploads to test S3/GCS buckets and retention hints in Console (2 weeks)
Pilot: 2 customers (one AWS VPC with STS, one air-gapped on-prem using presigned URLs) for 4 weeks. Monitor DLQ rates, error classes, and throughput.
Canary: enable for 10% of new Private deployments region-by-region with telemetry gating for failure rates.
GA: full launch with docs, SDK/agent binary, and Console integration. Customer onboarding runbook published.
Rollback: disable sink at tenant level and keep last 7 days of buffered files in DLQ to allow replays; provide manual replay tooling to customer support.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation, per-chunk checksum validation, and NDJSON compliance.
Integration tests using localstack, gcs emulator, azure storage emulator to validate connector flows.
Chaos tests: simulate network partitions and S3 5xx errors to verify backoff and DLQ behavior.
Perf tests: validate throughput at expected tenant loads (target 10k events/sec per node) and document cost estimates for batching/granularity tradeoffs.
Security tests: pen-test for credential handling, cert rotation flows, and RBAC enforcement.
CI job: nightly e2e exports to a test bucket with artifact retention for 30 days.
migration_notes: Existing customers using legacy 'log-exporter' must opt into the VPC Audit Bridge. Migration script will translate legacy sink configs to new manifest-based sinks and schedule a test upload window.
For customers currently using Redwood-managed buckets, provide an export-only mode to copy historical logs to customer storage over a signed transfer job; rate-limited and quoted separately.
Documented rollback: if a customer's new sink fails, revert to current in-cluster retention and surface a ticket with support and engineering for manual replay.
open_questions: Should Redwood support server-side encryption using customer KMS keys for direct uploads, or require customers to enable storage provider-side encryption and pass encryption metadata? (security wants KMS support)
What is the maximum supported single-upload file size for presigned uploads in air-gapped mode before we enforce chunking? (proposal: 128MB)
Do we require a mandatory manifest signing scheme for customers who disable onboarded KMS? (proposal: yes, ephemeral HMAC)
What console UX is required for cert rotation for mTLS endpoints vs. letting customers rotate outside of Console?
